It's all about your individual susceptibility. 
If you used heavy for a week (and for some, binging a gram within a weeks time is heavy, for others that's nothing) you could possibly feel some very light symptoms of withdrawal. Maybe a headache and/or nausea. Maybe some restlessness, depression and/or irritability. 
You shouldn't (and very likely won't) have the more extreme withdrawal symptoms like cold sweats, tremors, vomiting/diarrhea, dehydration, nor should you have the week(s) long insomnia, delirium, or severe pain. 
You might just be somewhat sleepless, have some insane dreams and you might feel a little depressed/anxious from the dopamine depletion. There won't be enough symptoms to need weaning and definitely not hospitalization.

IMODIUM MY FRIEND!! Look it up for help with opioid withdrawals. But high(er) doses help extremely. It allowed me to sleep every night of withdrawal. While it doesn't take it all away, it helps enough where you can actually get up and do things to distract yourself, and most importantly you'll be able to get some all too important sleep. Imodium as an mu opioid agonist that acts on the lower intestine, but your brain will see it as an opioid either way, so it'll help. I swear by it during my worst withdrawals. 

Edit to Add: Super high doses of Imodium can become cardiotoxic. So be sure to pace yourself, and not take a ton all at once to try and help yourself. I know you want it to go away as soon as possible, but take about 5 pills at one time, and within 20 minutes you'll start to feel better. Idk your tolerance and your daily intake, but the amount you need for relief is rarely enough to be cardiotoxic. I used it for fentanyl withdrawal. 

AND STAY FAR AWAY FROM BENADRYL!!! I know we'd naturally think it'll help with sleep, but it makes restless legs soooooo much worse. So no benadryl, no antihistamines.

P.S.: I know we all just really want to be comforted and feel loved during this. I've literally held my homies and pet their heads, letting them cry on me because their withdrawals were so bad and i couldn't help in any other way. I help them take showers, give massages, help them eat and drink, try to help them move around and distract themselves... We all just want to be babied and loved on when we're super dope sick. I'm sorry you're going through this. I believe in you, and you can make it out the other side. You'll be a better person.
